package_metadata.purpose: V2 records for classes, prototypes, subclassing, ES modules, and CommonJS.

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: JavaScript class syntax is modern syntax over prototype-based objects.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: class declarations define constructor functions and prototype methods. Instance state is initialized in constructors or fields. Inheritance uses prototype chains and super. Class bodies are strict.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: class C { constructor(x){ this.x=x } method(){} } new C(1)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Class syntax improves readability but does not erase prototype, this, or object-reference semantics.
common_use: Use subclassing where substitutability is clear
common_misuse: Assuming class methods are copied per instance
Using instance arrow fields for every method without memory/identity reason
Treating private state, prototype methods, and closures as identical
debugging_symptoms: Subclass method cannot access super as expected
safe_refactor_notes: Move methods between prototype and instance only after checking this binding and identity
Avoid subclassing refactors without tests for constructor/super order

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Subclasses extend behavior while relying on superclass initialization and methods.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: extends sets up prototype inheritance. Derived constructors must call super before using this. super.method resolves against the superclass prototype in method context.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: class D extends B { constructor(){ super(); } method(){ return super.method(); } }
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Subclass bugs often involve initialization order, method override contracts, and this/prototype expectations.
common_misuse: Assuming super is a dynamic property read from this
tests_or_checks: Test constructor arguments and superclass invariants
safe_refactor_notes: Prefer composition if subclass contract is unclear
Do not reorder super and this initialization casually

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: ES modules define explicit imports and exports with static structure.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: import/export declarations are parsed statically. Module code is strict. Bindings are live where specified by module semantics. Loading behavior depends on host environment and configuration.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: import x from "m"; import {y} from "m"; export default value; export {name}; <script type="module">
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Modules improve boundaries but create loader, file-type, and interop decisions across browser, Node, bundlers, and tests.
common_use: Organize browser or Node code with explicit dependencies
common_misuse: Mixing require/module.exports in ES module without interop plan
Assuming default import shape matches CommonJS export
debugging_symptoms: Works under bundler but not Node/browser directly
tests_or_checks: Identify host loader and package config
Run minimal import test in target runtime
safe_refactor_notes: Treat module conversion as runtime-boundary refactor
language_semantics_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host loaders

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: CommonJS is Node’s historical module system built around require and module.exports.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: A CommonJS module exports by assigning to exports or module.exports and imports synchronously with require. Interop with ES modules depends on Node/tooling behavior that must be verified for the current runtime.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: const x = require("x"); module.exports = value; exports.name = value
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Legacy Node packages and tools often use CommonJS, so review must check module shape and loader configuration.
common_use: Load JSON or built-in modules in legacy style
common_misuse: Assuming named ES imports work from all CommonJS packages
tests_or_checks: Test import/require both sides if interop
safe_refactor_notes: Do not rewrite require to import without runtime/tool tests
